tool_input.command: cat BenchPlugin.csproj Collection.cs; ls ~/.nuget/packages | grep -i betta; ls ~/.nuget/packages/betta*/*

result:
I changed Remap in `Remap.cs` as you described, and `dotnet build` succeeds with no warnings.

- **Rename:** the input "Value" is now "Number".
- **Clamp:** there is a new boolean input "Clamp" (default false). When true, the result is limited to the target range, and this also works when Target Min is greater than Target Max.
- **Outputs:** Remap now returns `(double Result, double Normalized)`, so it has two outputs. "Normalized" is the input's position in the source range, 0–1. It is not clamped, so it can fall outside 0–1 when the input is outside the source range. It is 0 when the source range is empty.
- **Subcategory:** the component is now in "Mapping" (set with `SubCategory = "Mapping"` on `[GrasshopperMethod]`). The "Bench" category is unchanged.

**Saved `.gh` files:** I did not pin the GUID, so existing saved `.gh` files will likely lose this component. The GUID changes with the signature, and I couldn't read the current one because it only shows up in Grasshopper (the Betta Inspector component lists it). I didn't invent one, as `CLAUDE.md` says not to. To keep saved files working, get the GUID from the old build and add `Guid = "…"` to the `[GrasshopperMethod]` attribute. If you paste the GUID here, I'll add it.
